_comment: Deterministic BLOCKING rules for the pre-publish tell gate. A match hard-blocks a push, so this file is kept DELIBERATELY SMALL: only unambiguous tells with a validated near-zero false-positive rate belong here. Everything judgment-shaped (title case, hype vocabulary, negative parallelism, decorative emoji, rule-of-three, en-dash-as-em) is handled by the Voice review dimension and the rewriting pass, against references/voice/ai-tells-catalog.md. Regexes are JS RegExp sources; \u escapes keep this file ASCII so it never flags itself. Optional per-rule 'dirs' narrows a rule to particular directories.
_scanning: scanDirs and scanExt normally come from review.config.json, which wins over anything set here. They are absent from this template on purpose: a rules file that shipped with directories in it would start blocking pushes in a repo that never chose to scan anything. Set publishGate.scanDirs in review.config.json to switch the gate on.
_adopting: These three rules encode one house style: straight ASCII punctuation, no em-dashes. That is a real editorial position and not a universal law. Delete any rule you disagree with rather than working around it, because a blocking rule nobody believes in gets bypassed with --no-verify, and that habit costs you the review receipt too.

rules.message: Em-dash (U+2014) found. The flagship AI tell. Rewrite the sentence so no dash is needed (split into two sentences, or fold the aside into the main clause). Never swap it for a comma or an en-dash. (Note: en-dash in a numeric range like 9-5 is fine and is NOT flagged.)
Spaced double-hyphen ( -- ) used as an em-dash. Same interrupt-and-restate tell wearing a thinner mark. Rewrite so no dash is needed.

Curly/smart quote or apostrophe found in authored content. A paste-from-model fingerprint in a straight-quote repo. Normalize to straight ASCII (' and "). If your rendering layer uses typographic quotes deliberately, narrow this rule with a 'dirs' key rather than deleting it.
